question: A cricketer has an average of 68 runs over 9 innings. If he scores 130 runs in the 10th inning, by how many runs (rounded off to the nearest whole number) does his average score increase?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Old average = 68 → total runs = 68 × 9 = 612

New total = 612 + 130 = 742

New average = 742 ÷ 10 = 74.2

Increase = 74.2 − 68 = 6.2 ≈ 6

**∴ Answer = 6 runs**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Average after 9 innings = 68, Score in 10th inning = 130

**Formula used:**

Average = Total runs ÷ Number of innings

**Calculation:**

⇒ Total runs in 9 innings = 68 × 9 = 612

⇒ Total runs in 10 innings = 612 + 130 = 742

⇒ New average = 742 ÷ 10 = 74.2

⇒ Increase in average = 74.2 − 68 = 6.2

⇒ Rounded off = 6

**∴ The correct answer is 6 runs.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Formula

Average = Total ÷ Number of observations

Updating Average

New total = Old total + new value

Effect of High Score

If new score > average, average increases.

Rounding Rule

Round to nearest whole number.
